The *Maṇithūṇavimānavatthu* ("Mansion with Pillars of Gems", Vv 77) is a canonical verse text preserved within the *Vimānavatthu* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts an encounter with a celestial deva who explains his past religious offerings and elucidates the heavenly rewards and fruits resulting from his deeds [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents 164 shared passages between this work and 23 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. It is commented upon extensively in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which contains 70 matches spanning §0.4–6.3 [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic and thematic parallels are widely distributed across the *Vimānavatthu* itself, with substantial verse correspondences found in the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dvārapālavimānavatthu* (Vv 55), *Nandanavimānavatthu* (Vv 76), *Cittalatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 75), and *Dutiyanāgavimānavatthu* (Vv 61) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus notes minor alignments with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (Taishō 100), though these remain computational matches rather than established parallels [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
